cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — IUSTA POSSESSIO, interdicts, civil possession
cards.front: Which two qualifications strengthen the possessor's legal position?
cards.back:
1. IUSTA POSSESSIO (unflawed possession) → protection of possession by interdicts (POSSESSIO AD INTERDICTA).
2. POSSESSIO EX IUSTA CAUSA (civil possession, POSSESSIO CIVILIS) → possession based on a valid title.
cards.old_front: Welche zwei Qualifikationen stärken die Rechtsstellung des Besitzers?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — IUSTA POSSESSIO, interdicts, civil possession
cards.front: What is IUSTA POSSESSIO?
cards.back:
Possession obtained from the opponent neither by force (NEC VI), nor secretly (NEC CLAM), nor by revocable grant (NEC PRECARIO).
• Prerequisite for protection by interdicts → hence also called POSSESSIO AD INTERDICTA.
cards.old_front: Was ist IUSTA POSSESSIO?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — IUSTA POSSESSIO, interdicts, civil possession
cards.front: What are possessory interdicts and what is their purpose?
cards.back:
Orders issued by the PRAETOR in individual cases to prevent dispossession or unauthorised interference.
• Aim: to keep threatened or open conflicts over possession from escalating.
• Only provisional — the right in rem itself is enforced only by the petitory action (ACTIO IN REM).
cards.old_front: Was sind Besitzinterdikte und welchen Zweck haben sie?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — IUSTA POSSESSIO, interdicts, civil possession
cards.front: What is the EXCEPTIO VITIOSAE POSSESSIONIS?
cards.back: The part of the interdict formula that denies protection to the INIUSTUS POSSESSOR — whoever possesses VI, CLAM or PRECARIO in relation to the opponent is not protected against him.
cards.old_front: Was ist die EXCEPTIO VITIOSAE POSSESSIONIS?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — IUSTA POSSESSIO, interdicts, civil possession
cards.front: In what sense is possessory protection relative (ALTER AB ALTERO)?
cards.back:
IUSTA/INIUSTA POSSESSIO is never established objectively, but only in relation to the opponent who also claims the thing.
• Eg: the thief is IUSTUS POSSESSOR towards everyone except the victim of the theft — if the thing is robbed from him, he is protected against the robber.
cards.old_front: Inwiefern ist der Besitzschutz relativ (ALTER AB ALTERO)?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — IUSTA POSSESSIO, interdicts, civil possession
cards.front: Prohibitory vs restitutory interdicts — what is the difference?
cards.back:
Prohibitory: forbid force against the IUSTUS POSSESSOR — “VIM FIERI VETO” (I forbid the use of force).
Restitutory: order the opponent to restore the thing — “RESTITUAS” (you shall restore).
• The EXCEPTIO VITIOSAE POSSESSIONIS applies to both: no one can demand the return of a thing that he himself took from the current possessor VI, CLAM or PRECARIO.
cards.old_front: Prohibitorische vs restitutorische Interdikte — Unterschied?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — IUSTA POSSESSIO, interdicts, civil possession
cards.front: May one use force against an INIUSTUS POSSESSOR?
cards.back:
Yes — whoever took the thing from his opponent VI, CLAM or PRECARIO is not protected against him and must tolerate its forcible recapture: VIM VI REPELLERE LICET.
• Under certain circumstances the IUSTUS POSSESSOR, too, may use force against the attacker.
• A rare case of permitted self-help in Roman law.
cards.old_front: Darf man sich gegen einen INIUSTUS POSSESSOR mit Gewalt wehren?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — IUSTA POSSESSIO, interdicts, civil possession
cards.front: Examples 6/7 (Leo and Thisbe): Leo threatens to drive Thisbe off her farm, and then does so. What is the position regarding interdicts?
cards.back:
Before the eviction: Thisbe possesses NEC VI NEC CLAM NEC PRECARIO → IUSTA POSSESSIO in relation to Leo; an interdict forbids him any use of force (VIM FIERI VETO).
After the eviction: Leo possesses VI in relation to Thisbe → flawed; the prohibition of force does not protect him, even if Thisbe takes the farm back by force (VIM VI REPELLERE LICET).
cards.old_front: Beispiele 6/7 (Leo und Thisbe): Leo droht Thisbe, sie von ihrem Hof zu vertreiben, und tut es dann. Interdiktenlage?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — IUSTA POSSESSIO, interdicts, civil possession
cards.front: Example 1 (Clara/vase with Leander): Can Clara recover her stolen vase from Leander by interdict? What if she takes it from Leander by force?
cards.back:
No — Leander's possession is unflawed in relation to her (he did not obtain the vase from her VI/CLAM/PRECARIO).
• If she takes it by force, she possesses VI in relation to Leander → Leander obtains an interdict against her (although she is the owner).
• She would have an interdict only against the thief Hector (he possessed CLAM in relation to her). Her remedy against Leander: ACTIO IN REM (REI VINDICATIO).
cards.old_front: Beispiel 1 (Clara/Vase bei Leander): Kann Clara ihre gestohlene Vase per Interdikt von Leander zurückholen? Was, wenn sie sie Leander gewaltsam wegnimmt?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — IUSTA POSSESSIO, interdicts, civil possession
cards.front: Which natural possessors (detentors) exceptionally enjoy protection by interdicts?
cards.back:
Emphyteutic lessees (Emphyteuta), precarists, pledgees and sequesters.
• They can defend their possession or recover possession they have lost.
• SEQUESTER = custodian of a disputed thing who hands it over to the winning party after judgment.
cards.old_front: Welche natürlichen Besitzer (Detentoren) genießen ausnahmsweise Interdiktenschutz?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — IUSTA POSSESSIO, interdicts, civil possession
cards.front: What is civil possession (POSSESSIO EX IUSTA CAUSA, POSSESSIO CIVILIS)?
cards.back: Possession based on a valid title (IUSTA CAUSA) — any transaction aimed at transferring ownership, eg sale, donation, loan, constitution of a dowry (DOS).
cards.old_front: Was ist Zivilbesitz (POSSESSIO EX IUSTA CAUSA, POSSESSIO CIVILIS)?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — IUSTA POSSESSIO, interdicts, civil possession
cards.front: What twofold advantage does civil possession bring?
cards.back:
a. If acquired from the entitled person on the basis of a IUSTA CAUSA TRADITIONIS, the possessor at the same time acquires ownership.
b. If acquired from an unauthorised person on the basis of a IUSTA CAUSA USUCAPIONIS, he may under certain circumstances acquire ownership by usucaption.
cards.old_front: Welchen zweifachen Vorteil bringt der Zivilbesitz?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — IUSTA POSSESSIO, interdicts, civil possession
cards.front: Example 1: Which of Hector (thief), Ago (antique dealer) and Leander (art dealer) has civil possession of Clara's vase, and does Leander become owner?
cards.back:
Leander has civil possession (sale = IUSTA CAUSA TRADITIONIS), as does Ago, provided he was not a receiver of stolen goods; Hector never does (no title).
• Leander does not become owner: Ago was neither owner nor authorised to dispose.
• Nor can he usucapt: stolen things (RES FURTIVAE) cannot be usucapted.
• Variant: if Clara herself sells and delivers, Leander becomes owner.
cards.old_front: Beispiel 1: Wer von Hector (Dieb), Ago (Antiquar) und Leander (Kunsthändler) hat Zivilbesitz an Claras Vase, und wird Leander Eigentümer?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — Excursus: FURTUM
cards.front: What is FURTUM?
cards.back:
Whoever takes another's movable thing with intent to enrich himself commits FURTUM.
• Broader than modern theft: it also covers eg embezzlement (Example 8: depositary Diogenes sells Iris' vase) and theft by finding (Example 9: Agatha keeps Carfinia's bracelet).
cards.old_front: Was ist FURTUM?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — Excursus: FURTUM
cards.front: What role does DOLUS play in FURTUM?
cards.back:
DOLUS (MALUS) = intent to enrich oneself when knowingly taking another's property; an essential element — without it, no theft.
• The thief acts “with DOLUS”.
cards.old_front: Welche Rolle spielt DOLUS beim FURTUM?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — Excursus: FURTUM
cards.front: Does a depositary already commit FURTUM when he decides to keep the deposited thing?
cards.back:
No — mere intent is not enough, even if the thing is already in his care. FURTUM arises only once the intent manifests itself in an external act, eg when he hides the thing with intent to enrich himself (Paulus (Sabinus, Cassius) D 41.2.3.18, Case 16).
• The intent to steal corresponds to the ANIMUS REM SIBI HABENDI; with the act of taking, ANIMUS and CORPUS are fulfilled → the thief becomes possessor.
cards.old_front: Begeht ein Verwahrer schon FURTUM, wenn er beschließt, die verwahrte Sache zu behalten?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — Excursus: FURTUM
cards.front: What is the thief's position as regards his possession?
cards.back:
He becomes possessor (ANIMUS + CORPUS), but his possession is unlawful (no IUSTA CAUSA) and flawed in relation to the victim (CLAM).
• He never acquires ownership.
cards.old_front: Welche Stellung hat der Dieb hinsichtlich seines Besitzes?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — Excursus: FURTUM
cards.front: Is FURTUM of land possible? How does the law protect against the forcible appropriation of land?
cards.back:
No — FURTUM only of movable things.
• Similar consequences: the LEGES IULIAE ET PLAUTIAE prohibit the usucaption of land appropriated by force, just as the LEX ATINIA prohibits the usucaption of stolen movables.
cards.old_front: Ist FURTUM an Grundstücken möglich? Wie schützt das Recht vor gewaltsamer Aneignung von Land?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — Excursus: FURTUM
cards.front: Which two actions does the victim of theft have against the thief?
cards.back:
1. ACTIO FURTI — penal action: penalty paid to the victim, fourfold the value for FURTUM MANIFESTUM (open theft), twofold for FURTUM NEC MANIFESTUM.
2. CONDICTIO FURTIVA — reipersecutory action, ie an action for recovery of the thing or its value.
cards.old_front: Welche zwei Klagen hat der Bestohlene gegen den Dieb?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — Excursus: FURTUM
cards.front: Against whom is the CONDICTIO FURTIVA directed — and does it presuppose that the thing still exists?
cards.back:
Only against the thief himself (not an ACTIO IN REM) — not against uninvolved third parties who possess the thing.
• It also applies if the thief no longer possesses or the thing has perished.
• An exception among the enrichment condictiones: the victim has not deliberately conferred anything on the thief.
cards.old_front: Gegen wen richtet sich die CONDICTIO FURTIVA — und setzt sie voraus, dass die Sache noch existiert?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — Excursus: FURTUM
cards.front: CONDICTIO FURTIVA vs REI VINDICATIO in cases of theft — advantages and disadvantages?
cards.back:
REI VINDICATIO: against any possessor of the stolen thing, but only as long as the thing exists.
CONDICTIO FURTIVA: only against the thief, but also without possession and after the thing has perished.
cards.old_front: CONDICTIO FURTIVA vs REI VINDICATIO beim Diebstahl — Vor- und Nachteile?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — Excursus: FURTUM
cards.front: Which actions can the victim of theft cumulate?
cards.back:
Penal and reipersecutory actions can be cumulated → ACTIO FURTI + CONDICTIO FURTIVA.
• CONDICTIO FURTIVA and REI VINDICATIO are both reipersecutory → they cannot be cumulated; the owner must choose.
cards.old_front: Welche Klagen kann der Bestohlene kumulieren?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — Excursus: FURTUM
cards.front: Who besides the owner is entitled to sue in case of FURTUM?
cards.back:
• The pledgee whose pledge was stolen: ACTIO FURTI (limited right in rem + economic interest; cf Paulus (Cassius) D 41.3.4.21, Case 74).
• Detentors contractually liable for theft (eg the launderer for the laundry): ACTIO FURTI, if they are solvent.
• The CONDICTIO FURTIVA remains with the owner; he must cede it to the holder after being compensated.
cards.old_front: Wer außer dem Eigentümer ist bei FURTUM klagebefugt?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — Retaining and losing possession: principles, movables, SERVUS FUGITIVUS
cards.front: What does retaining possession require; when does possession end?
cards.back:
As with acquisition: ANIMUS and CORPUS. Possession ends when the possessor gives up the intent to possess or loses all factual control.
• The jurists are less strict with retention than with acquisition.
• In the case of the SERVUS FUGITIVUS and of land, possession can be retained SOLO ANIMO for a limited time even after complete loss of CORPUS.
cards.old_front: Was verlangt die Erhaltung des Besitzes; wann endet er?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — Retaining and losing possession: principles, movables, SERVUS FUGITIVUS
cards.front: How can possession end — voluntarily and involuntarily?
cards.back:
Voluntarily: by handing the thing over to another (TRADITIO) or by unilateral abandonment.
Involuntarily: by loss of all control — or, with possession SOLO ANIMO, if control is not re-established after a certain time.
cards.old_front: Wie kann Besitz enden — freiwillig und unfreiwillig?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — Retaining and losing possession: principles, movables, SERVUS FUGITIVUS
cards.front: Does someone who throws goods overboard in distress at sea also lose ownership?
cards.back: No — he loses possession, not ownership; whoever gives up possession does not necessarily intend to give up ownership.
cards.old_front: Verliert, wer bei Seenot Ware über Bord wirft, auch das Eigentum?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — Retaining and losing possession: principles, movables, SERVUS FUGITIVUS
cards.front: Does someone who involuntarily loses possession remain owner? What about the finder?
cards.back:
Mostly yes: stolen movables and land appropriated by force cannot be usucapted — not even by later bona fide acquirers (possible again after REVERSIO AD DOMINUM).
• Whoever finds an obviously lost thing and intends to keep it is a FUR.
• A mere possessor could acquire ownership only by irreversible processing (SPECIFICATIO).
• If a wild animal regains its natural freedom, possession AND ownership are lost.
cards.old_front: Bleibt Eigentümer, wer den Besitz unfreiwillig verliert? Was gilt für den Finder?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — Retaining and losing possession: principles, movables, SERVUS FUGITIVUS
cards.front: By which criteria is the retention of possession assessed for movable vs immovable things?
cards.back:
Movable things: possession only as long as CUSTODIA (custody/control) exists — exception SERVUS FUGITIVUS.
Immovable things: in two cases also SOLO ANIMO:
  aa. without detentors/possessor's agents (eg absence)
  bb. where the possessor has appointed a detentor/possessor's agent.
cards.old_front: Nach welchen Kriterien wird die Erhaltung des Besitzes bei beweglichen vs unbeweglichen Sachen beurteilt?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — Retaining and losing possession: principles, movables, SERVUS FUGITIVUS
cards.front: What basic tendency does Roman law follow in retaining possession?
cards.back:
Existing possessory situations are to be preserved and hasty changes prevented — a change of possession only if it is likely to be permanent.
• a. TRADITIO is a legal transaction (acquirer lacking legal capacity).
• b. Where involuntary loss threatens, possession is upheld for as long as possible (land: as long as another's control appears temporary, Iavolenus D 41.2.22, Case 55).
• Reason: a stable system, because a change of possession can lead to a change of ownership.
cards.old_front: Welche Grundtendenz verfolgt das römische Recht bei der Besitzerhaltung?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — Retaining and losing possession: principles, movables, SERVUS FUGITIVUS
cards.front: A thing is to be acquired by a mentally ill person, who therefore cannot acquire possession. Does the transferor lose his possession despite the handover?
cards.back:
Disputed.
• Ulpian D 41.2.34 pr (Case 44) et al.: No — the transferor intends to give up possession only on condition that the other party acquires it; since that condition fails, he remains possessor (TRADITIO as a legal transaction).
• Celsus D 41.2.18.1 (Case 43): the transferor gives up possession in any case; if the recipient does not acquire, the thing is without a possessor.
cards.old_front: Ein Geisteskranker soll eine Sache erwerben und kann daher keinen Besitz erwerben. Verliert der Übergebende trotz Übergabe seinen Besitz?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — Retaining and losing possession: principles, movables, SERVUS FUGITIVUS
cards.front: Can PUPILLI and FURIOSI give up their possession by mere intent (ANIMO)?
cards.back:
According to the prevailing view, not on their own authority — for their protection, their inner conviction is irrelevant.
• Abandonment only with AUCTORITAS TUTORIS or CURATORIS respectively.
• Where retention requires CORPUS, their possession ends with its loss, as with anyone else.
• Cf Ulpian D 41.2.29 (Case 41), Marcianus D 41.1.11 (Case 42), Proculus D 41.2.27 (Case 49).
cards.old_front: Können PUPILLI und FURIOSI ihren Besitz durch bloßen Willen (ANIMO) aufgeben?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — Retaining and losing possession: principles, movables, SERVUS FUGITIVUS
cards.front: What is CUSTODIA in the sense of retaining possession of movable things?
cards.back:
Factual control (CORPUS) over movables: it exists if one can lay hands on the thing at any time or bring it into one's immediate sphere of influence.
• Possession of movables continues as long as they are within the possessor's sphere of influence.
• In the law of obligations, CUSTODIA means something else (liability of the holder for loss, esp. theft).
cards.old_front: Was ist CUSTODIA im Sinne der Besitzerhaltung beweglicher Sachen?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — Retaining and losing possession: principles, movables, SERVUS FUGITIVUS
cards.front: Paulus D 41.2.3.13 (Case 46): Does one lose possession of a merely mislaid thing?
cards.back:
No — mislaid things remain within the possessor's sphere of influence, even if he temporarily cannot find them; CUSTODIA and possession continue.
• Different: whoever loses a thing outside his sphere of influence and does not know where it is loses possession (Pomponius D 41.2.25 pr, Case 45).
cards.old_front: Paulus D 41.2.3.13 (Case 46): Verliert man den Besitz an einer bloß verlegten Sache?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — Retaining and losing possession: principles, movables, SERVUS FUGITIVUS
cards.front: Ulpianus D 41.2.13 pr (Case 47): Stones are lost in the Tiber in a shipwreck and are later recovered from the riverbed. Possession and ownership?
cards.back:
Possession is lost (control lost), ownership is not.
• The text expressly distinguishes the SERVUS FUGITIVUS, possession of whom is retained.
cards.old_front: Ulpianus D 41.2.13 pr (Case 47): Steine gehen auf dem Tiber bei einem Schiffbruch verloren und werden später vom Flussgrund geborgen. Besitz und Eigentum?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — Retaining and losing possession: principles, movables, SERVUS FUGITIVUS
cards.front: Papinianus D 41.2.44 pr (Case 47a): Before a journey, A buries money and on his return no longer knows where. Does he still have possession?
cards.back:
Yes — as long as nobody intervenes, A retains control; his forgetfulness does not harm his possession, even if he buried the money on another's land.
• He has ANIMUS POSSIDENDI anyway; only control is in question.
cards.old_front: Papinianus D 41.2.44 pr (Case 47a): A vergräbt vor einer Reise Geld und weiß nach der Rückkehr nicht mehr, wo. Hat er noch Besitz?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — Retaining and losing possession: principles, movables, SERVUS FUGITIVUS
cards.front: Who possesses a SERVUS FUGITIVUS (runaway slave) — and why?
cards.back:
The master retains possession SOLO ANIMO (and continues to usucapt), although he has lost control — as long as no third party takes possession of the slave (Paulus D 41.2.1.14).
• The CUSTODIA criterion does not apply to slaves: strict confinement would impair their capacity for work, and valuable slaves should not be able to escape their master's control through cleverness.
cards.old_front: Wer besitzt einen SERVUS FUGITIVUS (entlaufenen Sklaven) — und warum?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — Retaining and losing possession: principles, movables, SERVUS FUGITIVUS
cards.front: Who possesses the things that a SERVUS FUGITIVUS took with him, and those he “acquires” while in flight?
cards.back:
Things taken with him: the master — the slave remains his possessor's agent.
Things acquired in flight: here, too, the master acquires possession through him.
• ANIMUS problem: no IUSSUM possible, a PECULIUM ends with the flight (Paulus D 15.1.48 pr) → probably solved by a fiction, as if he had acted within a valid PECULIUM.
• Purpose: protection of the master, who through the fugitive's transactions receives compensation for the resources he has lost.
cards.old_front: Wer besitzt die Sachen, die ein SERVUS FUGITIVUS mitgenommen hat, und die er auf der Flucht „erwirbt“?

cards.topic: 20.10. Possession II — Retaining and losing possession: principles, movables, SERVUS FUGITIVUS
cards.front: When does the master lose possession of the SERVUS FUGITIVUS? Can the new holder acquire through him?
cards.back:
When a third party seizes the slave.
• Bona fide third party (believes the slave has been derelinquished): from then on the slave can acquire possession for him.
• Mala fide third party: he cannot acquire possession through the slave (Paulus D 41.2.1.6, Case 28).
cards.old_front: Wann verliert der Herr den Besitz am SERVUS FUGITIVUS? Kann der neue Inhaber durch ihn erwerben?
